card: One prep rule table drives prompt, schema and checks; the gate is looser today
guard_cases: the_shipped_sample_still_passes_all_nine_checks (characters/malakor/prep.sample.json passes all nine checks unchanged; the existing the_sample_prep_passes_every_check_and_carries_its_results also still asserts its stored check details are exact)
deviations_from_card: Two commits: test(...) with the 3 compilable cases (2 red by assertion, 1 guard green), then feat(...) with rules.rs, the renderings, the tightened gate, the 3 drift tests that need the rules API (red before by non-compilation), and the doc rows. checks.rs re-exports the shared constants from rules (pub use) so other callers keep working; MIN_PREMISES/STORIES/CALLBACKS/STORY_LINES are gone (no users outside prep). The `shape` pass detail is unchanged on purpose: the shipped sample stores its check details, and the sample is outside the write set. The prompt wording now says 'with a payoff the host lands' for all three bit kinds (it used to say it only for premises).
notes: Gates were run on a clean `git archive HEAD` export in the scratchpad with my 6 files copied in (CARGO_TARGET_DIR in the scratchpad), because the shared checkout does not compile: crates/shadowrunr-reconcile/src/runs.rs has a non-exhaustive match on StreamEvent::LinkPinned from in-flight crates/shadowrunr-types/src/event.rs edits, and cargo fmt --check is red on shadowrunr-brain (character.rs, grammar.rs, rules.rs, tests.rs) and crates/shadowrunr-daemon/tests/cli.rs. These are sibling files (character-package A and others) that were dirty before this build started. Re-ran once in the real tree and saw the same reds, only in those paths. A gate run in the real tree should wait until they land. For slot B: checks.rs `shape` and `counts` now loop over rules::BITS (BitRule with count_ok/lines_ok/count_text/lines_text). Failure detail formats are kept ('{n} premises (at least 12)', '{id} is a story with {n} lines (2-5)'), and a callback with 0 lines now reads 'cb-NN is a callback with 0 lines (1-3)' instead of 'has no lines'.
